summary: PARTIAL is correct. #710 (60633eff3) is the only change in this area since f1be4abc7. It adds a Ryco-specific default port (7926) for fresh installs, persists the last served port in desktop-settings.json, refuses to persist one-launch fallbacks, and logs flips as a warning. Existing installs that already have a 'Local Storage' dir still start at 3773, the port T3 Code also uses, so they keep flipping to 3774/3775 whenever T3 Code starts first. That is the author's measured case, about 5.6% of launches. The app document is still loaded from http://127.0.0.1:<port>, so the origin is still tied to the port. A flipped launch now loses more than before: the primary last-known-shell IndexedDB cache from 45f7a9be6 is origin-scoped too, so the boot-paint shortcut goes cold. I found no other implementation: no Hub-side, renamed or ryco://-origin path. The auditor's fix-defect is real and somewhat broader than stated. The port record lives in ~/.ryco/userdata/desktop-settings.json, but the state it guards lives in Electron userData. Resetting or wiping ~/.ryco, an unreadable settings file, or a fresh install that never reaches backend-ready moves a 7926 install back to 3773. In the reset and never-ready cases it then persists 3773 for good.

evidence.note: DEFAULT_DESKTOP_BACKEND_PORT = 7926. Fresh installs no longer collide with T3 Code's 3773.
LEGACY_DESKTOP_BACKEND_PORT = 3773 is still the start port for every install that already has renderer state.
hasPriorDesktopRendererState is only existsSync(userData/'Local Storage'). resolveDesktopBackendStartPort returns the persisted port, else 3773 when that dir exists, else 7926.

shouldPersistDesktopBackendPort persists only when the preferred port served, or on a fresh install. A one-launch fallback to 3774 is deliberately not remembered, so the next launch retries 3773, and that launch's origin differs.

selectDesktopBackendPort probes 127.0.0.1, 0.0.0.0 and :: (main.ts:377-378) upward from the start port and logs 'warning: preferred backend port ... in use'. This covers the 'log the flip' part of the proposal.

persistDesktopBackendPort runs only from handleBackendReady, after the app was already loaded at bind time (loadPackagedBackendAppWindowOnBind, main.ts:1766-1770). Local Storage can exist before the port is recorded.
Persistence is skipped when desktopSettingsUnreadable is set or the write fails.
An unreadable desktop-settings.json falls back to defaults with backendPort null. A 7926 install then starts at 3773 and its origin flips.

desktop-settings.json (the port record) is under ~/.ryco/userdata. Local Storage is under Electron userData (resolveDesktopUserDataPath, set at main.ts:4614). The record and the state it protects live in different directories and can be reset independently.
window.loadURL(backendHttpUrl), also at main.ts:4587. The renderer origin is still http://127.0.0.1:<port>.

ryco:// is already registered as a privileged standard, secure, codeCache scheme. Its static file handler (main.ts:2196) and isDesktopAppUrl (main.ts:645) exist, but only the boot page is loaded from it. A port-independent origin is technically available but unused.
Composer drafts are still in origin-scoped localStorage, with attachment bytes in IndexedDB. A flipped launch still hides drafts.
New since the report (45f7a9be6): the last-known primary shell cache is IndexedDB keyed by window.location.origin, so a flipped launch also loses the cached boot paint.
Tests cover start-port resolution and persistence rules, but not migration and not a settings/userData mismatch.

remaining: 1) Existing installs still flip. An install with userData/'Local Storage' and no persisted port, or a persisted 3773, starts at 3773 (backendPort.ts:58-63, main.ts:4683-4690). When T3 Code holds 3773, Ryco serves on 3774 and does not persist it (backendPort.ts:80-88). That launch has a different origin, so localStorage drafts and UI state (composerDraftPersistence.ts:36-44, uiStateStore.ts:435), the IndexedDB attachment bytes, the primary shell cache (primaryShellCache.ts:72-95), and the HTTP and V8 caches are all cold or hidden. This is exactly the author's measured case. 2) The origin is still derived from the port: window.loadURL(backendHttpUrl) at main.ts:1757 and main.ts:4587. The long-term decoupling has not been done.
fixDefects: The port record is stored apart from the state it protects, and it is written late. resolveDesktopBackendStartPort trusts desktop-settings.json (~/.ryco/userdata, desktopPaths.ts:30-35) and uses existsSync(userData/'Local Storage') as the legacy signal (backendPort.ts:53-55). Any of these moves a post-#710 install from 7926 back to 3773 and strands its 7926 localStorage, IndexedDB and caches: (a) the user wipes or resets ~/.ryco, or uses a different RYCO_HOME, while Electron userData survives; (b) desktop-settings.json is unreadable, because defaults with backendPort null are used (main.ts:531-549) and persistence is skipped (main.ts:1640); (c) on a fresh install's first launch the app loads at bind time and creates Local Storage, but the backend never reaches handleBackendReady (main.ts:1618), so the port is never written. In (a) and (c), the next launch that serves 3773 persists it as preferred (backendPort.ts:86), so the move is permanent. Low frequency, but it is silent data loss of drafts on exactly the path the fix was meant to protect.
implementationSketch:
A. Fix defect (S, low risk). Keep the origin record next to the state it guards. Add readRendererOriginRecord/writeRendererOriginRecord in apps/desktop/src/backendPort.ts, backed by a small JSON file in Electron userData (e.g. app.getPath('userData')/renderer-origin.json, {version:1, port}), written atomically with mode 0600. In selectDesktopBackendPort (main.ts:4676), resolve persistedPort as record ?? desktopSettings.backendPort, which keeps the #710 field as a read fallback. When `persistable`, write the record synchronously right after selection, before any loadURL, instead of in handleBackendReady (main.ts:1618, 1636-1654). Then a crash before ready, a ~/.ryco wipe or unreadable settings can no longer reclassify the install. Optionally, keep mirroring into desktop-settings.json. Tests in backendPort.test.ts: the record overrides settings; a record present with an absent settings port still yields 7926; the legacy path applies only when there is no record and Local Storage exists.

B. Migrate existing installs off 3773 (M, medium risk; product decision). Do a one-time renderer-state export and import so legacy installs can move to the persisted Ryco port (7926). (1) Add a desktop bridge IPC pair, e.g. desktop:origin-state:export and desktop:origin-state:take, in apps/desktop/src (preload plus main), with a size cap. (2) In apps/web, in a desktop-only early module run before the zustand persist stores rehydrate (before composerDraftStore and uiStateStore are imported in main.tsx/__root), do this on a legacy-origin launch flagged by main: serialize all localStorage entries plus the composer attachment-bytes IndexedDB store, and send them to main. Main writes userData/origin-migration-v1.json (0600) and sets the renderer-origin record to 7926 for the next launch. Do not migrate the primary shell cache or the HTTP/V8 caches; they rebuild. (3) On the next launch at the new origin, the same early module calls take(), writes only keys that are absent, re-puts the attachment bytes, acks, and main deletes the bundle. If the import fails, keep the bundle and retry, and never delete the old origin's data. Tests: unit tests for the export/import merge (absent-only, size cap, idempotent ack) in apps/web/src/persistence; backendPort tests for the record transition; one desktop smoke test that a draft written on 3773 is visible after the move.

C. Long-term (L, needs decision). Load the shell from ryco://app instead of loadURL(backendHttpUrl) at main.ts:1757 and main.ts:4587. The scheme is already privileged and has a static handler (main.ts:338-349, 2196). The renderer would then reach the backend through the bridge-provided httpBaseUrl/wsBaseUrl. This needs backend CORS for ryco://app, auth that does not depend on same-origin cookies (bearer/ticket), CSP review, and the same one-time migration as B. After that, port flips only affect API and WebSocket traffic.
decisionReason: Moving existing installs to a new origin is a product trade-off about user data: drafts, UI state and attachment bytes must be migrated, or they are stranded. #710 deliberately chose not to move them. The long-term ryco://app origin changes same-origin, cookie and CORS assumptions between the desktop renderer and the backend, which is an auth-semantics change that needs review. Part A, the defect fix, is low risk and needs no decision.
